name: Dusty brown
lede: Dusty brown is a dark, muted olive-brown, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Rikancha, named for a particular tea master's taste rather than for dust.

sections.title: "Rikan brown," not dust
sections.body:
Rikancha (璃寛茶), literally "Rikan brown," is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for Rikan, though the page does not say who or what Rikan was; it is undocumented in the sources consulted here [1]. It is one of many *cha* (tea) names in the traditional list for muted browns, and the name has nothing to do with dust, despite its English rendering [1].

Its nearest named neighbor on file is [[seaweed-green]], 3.5 units off [2], an unrelated name that happens to land on nearly the same muted color.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in 5,144 of 23,781 paintings, 21.63 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 3,783 [3]. That makes it more common than 99 percent of the named colors in our library, one of the most frequent matches we track [3]. It peaks in the 1100s, present in 20.0 percent of our 50 paintings from that century, 1.4 times the museums' baseline rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 41 percent of its 3,783 appearances by lightness rank [3].

Meindert Hobbema is its most devoted painter on file, present in 9 of his 16 works here, more than three times the baseline rate for the museums that hold them [3]. The earliest match dates to the year 900, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It shares canvases with [[baiko-brown|Baiko brown]] and [[greyish-brown|Greyish Brown]] more often than chance [3]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [3].
